title: Long-range operators (q^-2, q^-4) versus the LZ event: a systematic map of which mediator masses and operator structures can leave a lone 248 keV recoil
question: For each NR operator dressed with one or two light-mediator propagators m^2/(m^2+q^2), which (operator, m_med) combinations keep N_lo = R(5.4-55 keV)/R(200-270 keV) <= 3-5 at 1 TeV, where does the contact regime end, how does light-mediator SI DM scale, and which term drives the photon-dipole N_lo = 376?
headline_result: Light mediators only soften spectra: no contact-excluded operator is rescued at any m_med; O6/O15/O9/O14/O10 keep N_lo <= 5 only for m_med >= 0.11/0.26/0.29/0.32/0.41 GeV (two propagators 0.22-0.61 GeV); every spectrum is contact-like (within x1.5) above 0.45-0.48 GeV (n=1) / 0.66-0.69 GeV (n=2) = 1.8-2.8 q(248 keV); light-mediator SI DM gives N_lo 3021-7.7e5 (0.1-1 GeV to q^-4), scaling m^-1.94; O6/q^2 collapses onto O4 (27.8 vs 28.1) but q^2-rate operators overshoot (O10/q^2 353); the photon dipole's 375 companions come from the c5 charge term (88% of R_lo) over the spin term's R_hi (89%), and a massive dark-photon dipole is compatible only for m >= 0.32 GeV
model_or_mechanism: NREFT operators O1, O3-O15 (isoscalar; O1 proton-only) x [m^2/(m^2+q^2)]^n, n=1,2, elastic, 1 TeV; photon/massive-vector magnetic dipole decomposition
confidence: high for the map and thresholds (coupling-independent ratios, validated factorisation); medium for the compatibility boundary (recalled 3-5 event tolerance)
